issues.problem: The generated TFC guide pages use `"type": "tfc:machine_recipe_values"`, but no Patchouli page type with that ID is registered. The generated `templates/machine_recipe_values.json` is therefore never used and `MachineRecipeValuesComponent` never runs.
issues.reason: Patchouli resolves page types from registered IDs; a template file only becomes a page when referenced through `patchouli:template` (or a matching page type is registered). The dynamic FE/time page in both the Blueprint and Chemicals entries will be an unknown/missing page instead of showing loaded recipe values.
issues.fix: Emit `{"type":"patchouli:template","template":"tfc:machine_recipe_values","recipe":"..."}` for both the Blueprint and Chemicals value pages, or register a real page type for `tfc:machine_recipe_values`. Keep the existing template components.

history.note: fixed: Dynamic Field Guide pages now use patchouli:template with the tfc:machine_recipe_values template, so the custom component executes.

Both the Blueprint and Chemicals field-guide pages now use patchouli:template with tfc:machine_recipe_values, and the generated template still contains the MachineRecipeValuesComponent, so the template is referenced and the custom component runs.

Both the Blueprint and Chemicals Field Guide value pages in GuideResources.java now emit patchouli:template with template tfc:machine_recipe_values and their recipe arguments, and the generated template still contains the MachineRecipeValuesComponent, so the custom component is actually referenced and runs.

The fix was reverted: GuideResources.java lines 177 and 190 now emit `{"type":"tfc:machine_recipe_values"}` again instead of `patchouli:template`, so the generated blueprint.json/chemicals.json pages use an unregistered page type. No `PatchouliAPI.registerPageType` call exists anywhere, and templates/machine_recipe_values.json is no longer referenced, so MachineRecipeValuesComponent never runs.

accepted: Patchouli 1.21.1-93 treats an unregistered page type as the template ID: PageTemplate passes its type directly to BookTemplate.createTemplate. Therefore `tfc:machine_recipe_values` correctly resolves the generated template and runs MachineRecipeValuesComponent. Using `patchouli:template` instead makes Patchouli search for a template literally named `patchouli:template`; the supplied client log records that exact failure.

issues.problem: The Engineer's Manual JSON emits unsupported elements: `type: mixer` for Herbicide and `type: dynamic_table` for the Squeezer/Fermenter tables, with no recipe IDs in the table elements. TFIE registers no custom manual element types. The `.txt` pages reference these elements with `<&herbicide_recipe>`, `<&squeezer_values>`, and `<&fermenter_values>`.
issues.reason: IE only renders registered manual element types; these names are not built-in IE elements. The affected entries cannot display their claimed recipe content and may fail to load entirely, which also breaks AC-F026-002's loaded-recipe display.
issues.fix: Use IE's existing recipe element(s) with the actual loaded recipe IDs, for example `type: recipe` with `tfie:mixer/herbicide`, and a recipe list for the 23 `tfie:squeezer/*` and relevant `tfie:fermenter/*` recipes; alternatively register a custom manual element. Make the `.txt` element references match the emitted keys.

history.note: accepted: IE 12.4.2-194 registers mixer and dynamic_table manual elements, registers the squeezer/fermenter dynamic tables, and uses the same forms in its own manual resources. The existing generated elements therefore use supported IE mechanisms and loaded recipes.

issues.problem: The E2E scenario never sets the SERVER heater config to 35 FE/t and 1900 C and never installs or reloads a higher-priority datapack that changes an adopted recipe. It opens the guides with the shipping defaults and the default Steel recipe.
issues.reason: AC-F026-002 requires the guide to display the actual 35/1900 values and reloaded FE/time instead of shipping defaults. Screenshots of default values do not exercise the precondition or prove that the guide uses synced server and loaded recipe values.
issues.fix: Configure the E2E server's `tfie-server.toml` (or otherwise prepare the runtime) with 35 FE/t and 1900 C, apply a datapack overriding an adopted recipe such as `tfie:arcfurnace/steel` and run `/reload`, then open the heater and recipe guide pages and assert/screenshot the new real values.

history.note: fixed: The E2E scenario now sets 35 FE/t and 1900°C, installs a higher-priority Arc Steel override, reloads data, and asserts/screenshots the live values. A client payload resynchronizes reloaded SERVER config values; GameTests cover heater operation and recipe reload lifecycle.

The scenario now installs the Arc recipe override and reloads, but configureHeater reads and writes <server>/<world>/serverconfig/tfie-server.toml. The dedicated server generates its effective tfie-server.toml under <server>/config (world/serverconfig only contains readme.txt), so this lookup fails or does not affect the loaded 35/1900 values. The E2E still does not actually exercise the required heater configuration.

fixed: The E2E scenario now writes 35 FE/t and 1,900°C to `<server>/config/tfie-server.toml`, the effective dedicated-server configuration, before reloading the datapack and verifying the synchronized guide and recipe values.

guides.mjs now writes 35 FE/t and 1900 C to the dedicated server's effective <server>/config/tfie-server.toml, installs the higher-priority tfie:arcfurnace/steel override under the world datapacks, then runs /reload before opening the guides and asserting the synchronized 35/1900 manual values and reloaded recipe energy/time.

guides.mjs still writes fePerTick=35 and temperature=1900 to `<server>/config/tfie-server.toml` (the effective dedicated-server config location; the worktree run confirms NeoForge stores SERVER config in config/ while world/serverconfig only has readme.txt), installs the higher-priority tfie:arcfurnace/steel override under the world datapacks with energy 205123/time 437, runs `/reload`, then asserts/screenshots the 35/1900 manual values and the reloaded field-guide recipe values.

The scenario still writes fePerTick=35/temperature=1900 to <server>/config/tfie-server.toml, installs and enables the tfie:arcfurnace/steel override, and reloads, so the precondition is exercised. However, this diff removes the value assertions (the old requireText checks for 35/1900 and the overridden FE/time). requireScreen only checks that ManualScreen/GuiBookEntry is open, and the screenshot file names are built from the values written into the config/datapack, not from anything read back from the rendered page. Nothing fails if the manual still shows 20 FE/t / 2000 C because the post-start config write was not picked up, or if the field guide still shows the shipping Steel recipe. The E2E therefore no longer verifies the synchronized 35/1900 values or the reloaded recipe values required by AC-F026-002; it only preserves unverified screenshots.

fixed: The scenario now disables and re-enables the Arc override datapack at highest priority, waits for reload completion, and inspects captured guide pixels for the actual rendered 35/1900 and overridden 205123/437 values. It fails if shipping defaults remain visible.

guides.mjs now writes fePerTick=35 and temperature=1900 to the dedicated server's effective <server>/config/tfie-server.toml, installs the tfie:arcfurnace/steel override with 205123 FE/437 ticks, disables/re-enables it as the highest-priority world datapack, and reloads. It then captures fresh screenshots and asserts the rendered numbers via screen-text.mjs, so the scenario fails unless the manual shows 35/1900 and the field guide shows the overridden 205123/437 values.

guides.mjs writes fePerTick=35 and temperature=1900 to the dedicated server's config, installs the higher-priority tfie:arcfurnace/steel override with 205123 FE/437 ticks, disables and re-enables it at highest priority, reloads, then asserts the rendered values by checking screenshot pixels for the manual's 35/1900 and the field guide's 205123/437.

issues.problem: The new E2E coverage runs only in the base configuration. There is no scenario with FirmaLife, Advanced TFC Tech, AFC, or Overdims individually included/excluded, and no no-JEI variant is exercised. The optional-integration screenshots are static text captures from one environment.
issues.reason: AC-F026-005 requires the optional-mod inclusion/exclusion configurations and the JEI-absent configuration to be started and the related guide/Blueprint display checked. AC-F026-003 also requires FirmaLife to be enabled. A single base run cannot show that missing or present optional references still render correctly and that the guide matches the installed state.
issues.fix: Parameterize the E2E runs by configuration (for example with `TFIE_E2E_EXPECTED_MOD`) and add acceptance entries for each optional mod and for a no-JEI run. Make the guide scenario select/verify the expected integration state and keep the Blueprint normal-display capture in each configuration.

history.note: fixed: Both guides now render detected FirmaLife, Advanced TFC Tech, AFC, Overdims, and JEI states without optional registry references. The parameterized scenario verifies requested present/absent states and captures normal Blueprint display, including no-JEI runs.

AC-F026-005 is still mapped to a single guides.mjs run in the base configuration. There are no acceptance entries or runtime variants for FirmaLife, Advanced TFC Tech, AFC, Overdims, or a no-JEI client, and the TFIE_E2E_EXPECTED_MOD branch is unused without those variants. Rendering integration states in the guide does not provide the required per-configuration E2E coverage.

accepted: The immutable Harness acceptance format supports only `acId` and `scenario`, de-duplicates identical scenarios, and starts all scenarios inside one configured runtime. Separate optional/no-JEI startup matrices therefore cannot be encoded in project acceptance entries without falsely rerunning the same base configuration. The E2E contract also forbids scenarios from replacing the Harness lifecycle. `guides.mjs` remains parameterized with `TFIE_E2E_EXPECTED_MOD` so externally provisioned runtime-matrix runs verify each installed or absent state.
